Class WhoSpringSecurityAutoConfiguration

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.who.autoconfigure.WhoSpringSecurityAutoConfiguration
@AutoConfiguration(after=WhoAutoConfiguration.class) @EnableConfigurationProperties(WhoProperties.class) @ConditionalOnClass(name="org.jwcarman.who.spring.security.WhoSessionSecurityContextRepository") public class WhoSpringSecurityAutoConfiguration extends Object
Wires who into Spring Security when who-spring-security is on the classpath: the session repository, GET /who/me, the exception hand-off, and method security so that @RequiresPermission is enforced (turn it off with who.method-security.enabled=false).

  • Method Details

    • whoSessionSecurityContextRepository

      @Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean public WhoSessionSecurityContextRepository whoSessionSecurityContextRepository(WhoService whoService, WhoSessions whoSessions, Clock clock, WhoEventPublisher whoEventPublisher, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<StatelessLoginMethod> statelessMethods)
      Keeps only a WhoSession (ids and the sign-in time) in the HTTP session and resolves the principal again on every request, so a deactivated identity or a revoked credential takes effect at once.
      Parameters:
      whoService - resolves the principal
      whoSessions - records each sign-in and says whether its session is live
      clock - stamps the sign-in time
      whoEventPublisher - publishes session events
      statelessMethods - the API-key and bearer-token methods, read on each request: a request that presents one's credential is never a browser session
      Returns:
      the repository

    • whoSessions

      @Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean public WhoSessions whoSessions(SessionRecordRepository repository, WhoEventPublisher whoEventPublisher, Clock clock, WhoProperties properties, org.springframework.core.env.Environment environment, org.springframework.core.io.ResourceLoader resourceLoader)
      who's record of browser sessions. The idle timeout is Spring Boot's: spring.session.timeout when set, else server.servlet.session.timeout, else 30 minutes.
      Parameters:
      repository - where sessions are kept
      whoEventPublisher - publishes ended and purged sessions
      clock - the current time
      properties - who's settings
      environment - where the timeout is read
      resourceLoader - tells whether Spring Session is present
      Returns:
      the sessions
